name: General Intuition
desc: Frontier AI research lab building agents and world models trained on video game footage from the Medal clip platform.
markets: Pre-revenue; testing a commercial agent product with a few robotics, simulation and entertainment customers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Heavily funded AI lab with gaming roots; F1 could showcase simulation and agent technology, but it has no consumer brand yet.

name: Hyperscale Data
desc: Holding company operating a Michigan AI data centre, bitcoin mining, lending, hotel and other businesses through subsidiaries.
markets: Operations in the United States: Michigan data centre campus, bitcoin mining, lending and hotel; no verified international operations.
rationale: Small-cap diversified holding with little brand marketing; weak F1 fit beyond possible publicity for its data-centre business.
changed: Formerly named Ault Alliance; Giga-tronics defence unit in Chapter 11 and deconsolidated

name: Lila Sciences
desc: Builds AI models and autonomous laboratories to run experiments in life sciences, chemistry and materials science.
markets: Pre-revenue; labs in Cambridge, Massachusetts; announced new hubs in San Francisco and London; no named customers yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue science AI lab with no consumer brand; a materials-science showcase is conceivable, but F1 fit is weak today.

name: ModelBest
desc: Develops efficient large language models, including the open-source MiniCPM series, for on-device use in phones and cars.
markets: Mainly China (device makers, carmakers, telecoms); Samsung smartphone partnership in South Korea; no verified wider customer base.
rationale: Chinese on-device AI supplier to phone and car makers; F1 could support technology branding, though the business is mostly B2B.

name: OLIX
desc: Develops optical tensor processing chips that use light to accelerate AI inference, with first deliveries targeted for 2027.
markets: Pre-revenue; based in London, hiring in Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco; first customer deliveries targeted for H2 2027.
rationale: Pre-revenue UK chip developer; an F1 technology showcase may suit later, but with no product or customers yet the fit is weak.

name: PaleBlueDot AI
desc: Provides GPU cloud compute and a marketplace for renting AI computing clusters hosted in third-party data centres.
markets: Customers and capacity in North America, Japan, South Korea and South-East Asia; US and Japan reported as main revenue sources.
rationale: Fast-growing AI compute provider across the US and Asia; F1 could build B2B brand awareness and hospitality with AI customers.

name: Recursive Superintelligence
desc: AI research lab developing self-improving systems that automate model design, training and evaluation; no product launched yet.
markets: Pre-revenue; teams in San Francisco and London; a public product launch was targeted for mid-2026, not confirmed.
rationale: Pre-revenue AI lab with a small team and no launched product; F1 fit is weak until it sells commercially.

name: Fortune Brands Innovations
desc: Makes home and security products including Moen faucets, Master Lock padlocks, Therma-Tru doors and Fiberon decking.
markets: About 84% of sales in the US and 8% in Canada; smaller sales in China, the UK and the EU.
rationale: North American home brands with modest overseas sales; F1 fit limited to US races, trade-customer hospitality and brand visibility.
changed: Renamed from Fortune Brands Home & Security to Fortune Brands Innovations

name: Edged US
desc: Builds and operates energy-efficient data centres for cloud and AI tenants, with campuses in Atlanta and Chicago.
markets: US campuses in Atlanta and Chicago; the separate Edged business in Spain and Portugal works with Merlin Properties.
rationale: B2B data-centre landlord with few customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality for large tenants.
changed: Formerly Edged Energy; part of Endeavour (not Telefonica as earlier noted)

name: Checkr
desc: Provides API-based background check and employment screening software for employers, staffing firms and gig platforms.
markets: Mainly US employers, with a Checkr Canada affiliate for Canadian checks; offers international screening covering 200+ countries.
rationale: US B2B HR-tech brand; F1 could support enterprise hospitality at US races, but international marketing need is limited.

name: GridPoint
desc: Provides energy management software and building controls that cut energy use for multi-site commercial businesses and utilities.
markets: Deployed in 20,000+ commercial buildings, focused on the US market; plans expansion into Japan and South Korea.
rationale: US B2B energy-efficiency software with a sustainability story; F1 sustainability messaging plausible, but marketing scale is small.

name: Cantina Labs
desc: Makes a consumer app for creating AI characters, chatting with them and friends, and producing character-led videos.
markets: Consumer app on Apple and Google app stores; user geography not confirmed; no verified international operations.
rationale: Consumer social AI app aimed at young users; F1 audience overlap is plausible, but scale and markets are unconfirmed.
changed: Reported to be a rebrand of the Airtime video-chat app

name: FintechOS
desc: Sells an AI-enabled low-code platform that banks, credit unions and insurers use to build and launch financial products.
markets: 60+ customers across North America, Europe and APAC; offices in London, New York, Bucharest and Amsterdam; fast US growth.
rationale: B2B fintech selling to banks and insurers in Europe and the US; F1 hospitality could support enterprise sales cycles.

name: Beacon Holdings (Beacon Software)
desc: Acquires small vertical software companies serving businesses such as campgrounds and construction firms, and adds AI to them.
markets: Portfolio of about 45 acquired software firms; their countries are not confirmed; no verified international footprint.
rationale: Software roll-up with many small brands and no single consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Handshake
desc: Runs a career network connecting university students and graduates with employers, and supplies expert data work to AI labs.
industry: student career network and AI data
markets: Mainly US universities; in the UK since 2020 with teams in Germany and France; employers from about 100 countries.
rationale: Reaches Gen Z students and graduate employers; F1 could support employer-brand and youth marketing in the US and Europe.
changed: Acquired Talentspace in 2022 and Uplimit in 2026; also acquired Cleanlab; launched Handshake AI in 2025

name: humans&
desc: AI research company building models and a product focused on communication and collaboration between people and AI.
markets: Pre-revenue; no product launched as of mid-2026; no verified international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue AI lab with no product or customers; weak F1 fit for now.

name: 2U
desc: Runs online degree, certificate and boot camp programmes for universities and operates the edX online learning platform.
markets: Degree partners mainly US universities; edX courses are offered online to learners abroad; country split not confirmed.
rationale: Education brand with a student audience; F1 tie-in weak given post-bankruptcy restructuring and university-led marketing.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in July 2024; restructured and left Nasdaq, now privately held

name: Armadin
desc: Develops an AI-native offensive security platform that runs automated attack campaigns to test enterprise and government defences.
markets: Unnamed Fortune 500 and government customers; partnerships with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike; no verified international operations.
rationale: Cyber peers such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler sponsor F1; founder Kevin Mandia's profile suits enterprise hospitality.

name: ASAPP
desc: Sells AI software for customer-service contact centres, including generative AI agents, to large consumer-facing companies.
markets: Customers mainly large US airlines, cable and telecom firms; offices in Buenos Aires and India besides US sites.
rationale: Enterprise AI vendor to US airlines and telecoms; rival Genesys sponsors F1; hospitality could aid enterprise sales.

name: Capacity
desc: Sells an AI support automation platform with chatbots, voice agents and knowledge tools for customer and employee service.
markets: Mainly US customers; owns UK businesses CereProc and YouCanBookMe; customer country split not confirmed.
rationale: Acquisitive US B2B software firm; F1 hospitality plausible for enterprise sales, though brand marketing is limited.
changed: Acquired many companies since 2023, including SmartAction and CereProc (2024), YouCanBookMe, KLaunch and Creovai (2025)

name: Datavault AI
desc: Develops AI data monetisation, tokenisation and ADIO audio technology, licensing it to media, sports and event partners.
markets: Mainly US partners in media, sports and events; announced a Swiss digital-asset exchange partnership in 2025.
rationale: Small-cap with sports tokenisation ambitions; F1 fit is speculative and the company is financially weak.

name: Dexterity
desc: Builds AI-powered robots, including the Mech system, that load and unload trucks and handle parcels in warehouses.
markets: Customers in the US (FedEx, UPS, GXO) and Japan (Sagawa Express); no verified European deployments.
rationale: Logistics robotics with US and Japan customers; F1 logistics and technology showcase possible, but B2B with modest marketing.

name: Factory
desc: Sells autonomous AI coding agents, called Droids, that write, test and fix code for enterprise engineering teams.
markets: Enterprise customers mainly in the US, plus Adyen and EY; EU-hosted option; London and Tokyo offices planned for 2026.
rationale: AI coding rivals such as Cognition and Vercel partner with F1; strong fit for technology showcase and enterprise hospitality.

name: FieldAI
desc: Develops hardware-agnostic autonomy software that lets robots operate in off-road, industrial, construction and mining sites.
markets: Offices in Irvine, San Francisco, Boston, Tokyo and Singapore; partnership with Caterpillar; customer countries not confirmed.
rationale: Robot autonomy firm with a Caterpillar tie-in; F1 technology showcase plausible, but B2B with limited brand marketing.
